CERT_ANCIENT_EGYPTIAN.name: Ancient Egyptian (Advanced Language Study)
CERT_ANCIENT_EGYPTIAN.description: Certificate of Advanced Language Study in Ancient Egyptian offered by the Department of Near Eastern Languages and Civilizations. A certificate adviser advises students on the certification process. The certificate is listed on the student's transcript once completed.
notes: No Credit/D/Fail
Letter grade B or above required in all courses
Declare candidacy on Yale Hub as early as possible, no later than January 15 or September 15 of final semester
With adviser approval, an advanced texts seminar and/or graduate seminar may count toward requirements
Up to two courses of credit-bearing academic study abroad may be substituted with prior permission

requirements.name: Courses beyond L3
requirements.description: Four courses beyond the L3 level in Ancient Egyptian. At least two must be Yale courses designated L5.

CERT_ANCIENT_GREEK.name: Ancient Greek (Advanced Language Study)
CERT_ANCIENT_GREEK.description: Certificate of Advanced Language Study in ancient Greek offered by the Classics Department to non-majors. A certificate adviser, typically the DUS, advises students on the certification process. The certificate is listed on the student transcript once certified.
notes: For non-majors only
No Credit/D/Fail
Letter grade B or above required in all courses
Declare candidacy on Yale Hub as early as possible, no later than January 15 or September 15 of final semester
With adviser approval, one course such as an independent study (graded pass/fail), graduate seminar, or advanced seminar may count
One LxC course taught in English may count if it includes a weekly discussion section conducted entirely in Greek (minimum three students; course designated LxC)
Up to two study-abroad credits taught in Greek may be substituted with adviser approval

requirements.name: Courses beyond L4
requirements.description: Four courses in ancient Greek beyond the L4 level (i.e., four L5 courses; 3000- or 4000-level Greek courses).

CERT_CHINESE.name: Chinese (Advanced Language Study)
CERT_CHINESE.description: Certificate of Advanced Language Study in Chinese offered by the Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures. A certificate adviser, typically the DUS, advises students on the certification process. The certificate is listed on the student's transcript once certified.
notes: No Credit/D/Fail
Letter grade B or above required in all courses
Courses conducted in English (e.g., CHNS 1700 and CHNS 1710) do not count
Declare candidacy on Yale Hub as early as possible, no later than January 15 or September 15 of final semester
With adviser approval, one advanced non-L5 course conducted in Chinese (e.g., independent study graded pass/fail, graduate seminar, or advanced seminar) may count
One LxC course taught in English may count if it includes a weekly discussion section conducted entirely in Chinese (minimum three students; course designated LxC)
Up to two study-abroad credits taught in Chinese may be substituted with adviser approval

requirements.name: Courses beyond L4
requirements.description: Four courses beyond the L4 level in Chinese. At least two must be Yale courses designated L5.

CERT_CLIMATE_SCIENCE.name: Climate Science and Solutions
CERT_CLIMATE_SCIENCE.description: Provides students with a foundation in basic climate science, anthropogenic climate change, and solutions, preparing them to be effective and informed leaders on one of humanity's grand challenges.
notes: Three of the six courses must have a science, engineering, or technology focus.
No more than two course credits may overlap with a major, simultaneous degree, or another certificate.
No course credit may be applied toward the requirements of more than two curricular programs.
No more than four credits may come from a single department or school.
No more than one course taken Credit/D/Fail or one independent study course graded pass/fail may count toward the certificate.

Courses taken at another institution or during an approved summer or term-time study abroad program may count with certificate director approval. An on-topic summer internship can replace one elective.
Declare on Yale Hub by January 15 or September 15 of the final semester at the latest.

requirements.name: Basic Climate Science
requirements.description: Course with YC Climate Basic Climate Sci attribute. Covers components, processes, and feedback of the climate system, including ocean-atmosphere dynamics, the carbon cycle, atmospheric gases, radiative balance, and spatial and temporal climate variability.

requirements.name: Anthropogenic Climate Change
requirements.description: Course with YC Climate Anthropogenic attribute. Covers drivers and projections for anthropogenic climate change, feedback and uncertainties in regional-to-global climate models, climate change impacts, mitigation, adaptation, and interactions with other aspects of global societal and environmental change.

requirements.name: Climate Solutions
requirements.description: Course with YC Climate Solutions attribute. Covers scientific, technological, and socio-political aspects of natural and technological solutions and strategies.

requirements.name: Climate seminar
requirements.description: Seminar on climate science and solutions as approved by the certificate director.

requirements.name: Additional electives
requirements.description: Remaining certificate-eligible courses. At least three of the six total courses must have a science, engineering, or technology focus.

CERT_COLLECTIONS.name: Collections: Objects, Research, Society
CERT_COLLECTIONS.description: Exposes students to expertise within Yale's special collections libraries, equipping them with analytical skills and methodologies that scholars, librarians, archivists, conservators, and curators employ to preserve and steward the human record across manuscripts, documents, film, audio, and digital formats.
notes: Minimum grade C in each course
No Credit/D/Fail
No more than two course credits may overlap with a major, simultaneous degree, or another certificate
No course credit may count toward more than two curricular programs
Approved graduate and professional school courses may count
Outside credit (study abroad, other institutions) or an on-topic summer internship may count with director approval
Declare on Yale Hub by January 15 or September 15 of the final semester; complete enrollment form on the Collections website

requirements.name: Introductory seminar
requirements.description: Required introductory seminar.

requirements.name: Capstone
requirements.description: Mandatory capstone culminating in a project focused on material histories (internship, research project, exhibit work, collections-intensive course, or other hands-on experience).

requirements.name: Primary collections area
requirements.description: Two courses in one of three areas: Research with Collections (YC Collections Research), Collections in Society (YC Collections Society), or Creative Critical Engagement with Collections (YC Collections Engagement).

requirements.name: Secondary collections area
requirements.description: One course in a different area from the primary area, drawn from the remaining two of: YC Collections Research, YC Collections Society, or YC Collections Engagement.

CERT_COMPUTING_CULTURE_SOCIETY.name: Computing, Culture & Society
CERT_COMPUTING_CULTURE_SOCIETY.description: Prepares students to understand the social, political, and historical implications of computing technology through a curated roadmap of courses across a dozen departments.
notes: Computer Science majors: in addition to the survey course, take four courses with at least one from each of categories 2–4 (categories 1 is for students without a computing background).
Non-Computer Science majors: in addition to the survey course, take one course from each of categories 1–4.
Each student must attend three critical computing-related lectures or events and submit a brief write-up to the certificate director.
CPSC 2265 / AMST 2265 may be replaced with another certificate-eligible course at the discretion of the certificate director.
All courses must be taken for a letter grade with a grade of C or above.
No courses taken Credit/D/Fail may be applied toward the certificate.
No more than two course credits may overlap with a major, simultaneous degree, or another certificate.
No course credit may be applied toward the requirements of more than two curricular programs.
Graduate and professional school courses may count toward the certificate.
Declare on Yale Hub by January 15 or September 15 of the final semester at the latest.

requirements.name: Survey course
requirements.description: Topics in Critical Computing.

requirements.name: Introduction to computing
requirements.description: Non-Computer Science majors only. Course with YC CSOC Introduction attribute.

requirements.name: Social research, politics, law, and economics
requirements.description: Course with YC CSOC Rsrch, Pltc, Law, Econ attribute.

requirements.name: History, digital media, and culture
requirements.description: Course with YC CSOC Hist, Media, Culture attribute.

requirements.name: Broader intersections in science, technology, and society
requirements.description: Course with YC CSOC Intersections attribute.

CERT_DATA_SCIENCE.name: Data Science
CERT_DATA_SCIENCE.description: Designed for students majoring in disciplines other than Statistics and Data Science to acquire knowledge for mature use of data analysis. Students gain skills to tackle real-world data analysis challenges in the humanities, social sciences, sciences, and engineering.
notes: Minimum grade B– in each certificate course
No course may satisfy both a major and the certificate
No single course may count toward two certificate areas
Declare intent by the last day of add/drop in the final term of enrollment on Yale Hub
Students are held to the Statistical Methodology and Data Analysis requirements in place when they declared; with DUS approval, updated 2024–2025 requirements may be fulfilled by prior declarers

requirements.name: Prerequisite
requirements.description: Suggested introductory course. An introductory data analysis course from another department may also satisfy this prerequisite.

requirements.name: Probability and Statistical Theory
requirements.description: Advanced students may substitute S&DS 3510, S&DS 3640, or ECE 4310.

requirements.name: Statistical Methodology and Data Analysis
requirements.description: S&DS 2200 and S&DS 2300 may not both count. ECON 2136 may be substituted for S&DS 2420.

requirements.name: Computation and Machine Learning
requirements.description: CPSC 3230 may be substituted for CPSC 2230.

requirements.name: Data Analysis in a Discipline Area
requirements.description: One course approved for this requirement and listed on the S&DS website.

CERT_EDUCATION_STUDIES.name: Education Studies
CERT_EDUCATION_STUDIES.description: Open to all interested Yale students, this certificate provides an opportunity to pursue an interdisciplinary study of education to complement their major.
notes: Successful completion of the certificate is noted on transcripts.
Courses taken Credit/D/Fail may not be applied toward the certificate.
No more than two course credits may overlap with a major, simultaneous degree, or another certificate.
No course credit may be counted toward the requirements of more than two curricular programs.
Graduate and professional school courses may count with approval from the Education Studies Associate Director.
Declare on Yale Hub once enrolled in EDST 1110; by January 15 or September 15 of the final semester at the latest.

requirements.name: Prerequisite
requirements.description: Foundational education studies course counted toward the five-course total.

requirements.name: Theory and Research
requirements.description: One course in Theory and Research as approved for the certificate. See Education Studies website for area listings.

requirements.name: Policy or Pedagogy
requirements.description: One course in either Policy or Pedagogy as approved for the certificate.

requirements.name: EDST electives
requirements.description: Two Education Studies electives as approved for the certificate.

CERT_EDUCATION_STUDIES_SCHOLARS.name: Education Studies Scholars Intensive
CERT_EDUCATION_STUDIES_SCHOLARS.description: A structured pathway for students interested in completing an Education Studies capstone project while learning alongside a supportive cohort from sophomore through senior year.
notes: Apply in the fall of sophomore year after completing or while enrolled in EDST 1110.
Field experience required as described on the Education Studies website.
Two of the five courses may overlap with the student's major.
No more than two course credits may overlap with a major, simultaneous degree, or another certificate.
No course credit may be counted toward the requirements of more than two curricular programs.
Credit/D/Fail courses may not count toward the certificate.
Graduate and professional school courses may count with approval from the Education Studies Associate Director.
Successful completion of the Scholar Intensive Certificate is noted on transcripts.

requirements.name: Prerequisite
requirements.description: Foundational education studies course counted toward the five-course total.

requirements.name: Theory and Research
requirements.description: Theory and Research requirement.

requirements.name: Policy or Pedagogy
requirements.description: One course in either Policy or Pedagogy as approved for the certificate.

requirements.name: Capstone seminar
requirements.description: Senior capstone seminar.

requirements.name: Capstone project
requirements.description: Senior capstone project course.

CERT_ENERGY_STUDIES.name: Energy Studies
CERT_ENERGY_STUDIES.description: Provides undergraduates with the knowledge and skills needed for advanced studies, leadership, and success in energy-related fields through coursework in three multidisciplinary tracks.
notes: ENRG 3000 is required as one of the six course credits (exceptions can be granted by the certificate director) and counts toward the Energy & Society track; take during junior or senior year.
ENRG 4000 (Senior Capstone Seminar) is optional but can count toward the six required credits in any one of the three tracks depending on project topic.
Language courses may not count toward the certificate.
No more than one course taken Credit/D/Fail or one independent study course graded Pass/Fail may count toward the certificate.
No more than two course credits may overlap with a major, simultaneous degree, or another certificate.
No course credit may be applied toward the requirements of more than two curricular programs.
Graduate and professional school courses and non-Yale courses accepted for full course credit by Yale College may count toward the certificate.
Declare on Yale Hub by January 15 or September 15 of the final semester at the latest.

requirements.name: Energy Science & Technology
requirements.description: Two courses in the Energy Science & Technology track as approved for the certificate.

requirements.name: Energy & Environment
requirements.description: Two courses in the Energy & Environment track as approved for the certificate.

requirements.name: Energy & Society
requirements.description: Two courses in the Energy & Society track as approved for the certificate. ENRG 3000 is required as one of the six total credits (exceptions may be granted by the certificate director).

CERT_ETHNOGRAPHY.name: Ethnography
CERT_ETHNOGRAPHY.description: Ethnography is both a set of qualitative research methods employed in the humanities and social sciences and a mode of presenting that research—in books and articles, film and video, embodied performance, and digital formats.
notes: Minimum grade C in each course
No Credit/D/Fail
At least four of six courses must be at the 3000-level or above
At least two courses must include substantial methods training and/or a practical ethnographic component, including at least one at the 3000-level or above
Attend two public talks or events featuring ethnography and submit one-page critical reflections on each
No more than two course credits may overlap with a major, simultaneous degree, or another certificate
No course credit may count toward more than two curricular programs
Approved graduate and professional school courses may count
Non-Yale courses may not count
Other courses may be approved by the certificate director
Declare on Yale Hub by January 15 or September 15 of the final semester

requirements.name: Ethnography methods courses
requirements.description: Courses with substantial methods training and/or a practical ethnographic component. Searchable in Yale Course Search with the YC Ethnography Methods attribute. At least one must be at the 3000-level or above.

requirements.name: Ethnography electives
requirements.description: Additional ethnography courses. Searchable in Yale Course Search with the YC Ethnography Elective attribute. At least four of the six total certificate courses must be at the 3000-level or above.

CERT_FOOD_AG_CLIMATE.name: Food, Agriculture, and Climate Change
CERT_FOOD_AG_CLIMATE.description: Prepares Yale College students for creative, critical, and unconventional engagement with pressing challenges facing food and agriculture at local and global scales, supported by the Yale Sustainable Food Program and Yale Farm.
notes: Students must participate in five co-curricular events identified by the YSFP and write a 6–8 page (double-spaced) summary reflecting a recurring theme, an area of controversy, and a proposed resolution.
No course taken Credit/D/Fail may be applied toward the certificate.
No more than two course credits may overlap with a major, simultaneous degree, or another certificate.
No course credit may be applied toward the requirements of more than two curricular programs.
Graduate and professional school courses may count toward the certificate.
Summer or year-abroad courses accepted for full Yale College credit may provisionally count with certificate director approval.
Declare on Yale Hub by January 15 or September 15 of the final semester at the latest.

requirements.name: Consumption
requirements.description: Two courses with YC Food Consumption attribute. Concerned with the broad practices of eating, nutrition and health, and cultural, historical, political, and economic dimensions of food.

requirements.name: Environment
requirements.description: One course with YC Food Environment attribute. Concerned with substrates and surroundings of food and agriculture, particularly those linked to processes of climate change.

requirements.name: Production
requirements.description: Two courses with YC Food Production attribute. Concerned with cultivation of plants for harvest as food, feed, fiber, and fuel, and husbandry or harvest of non-human animals destined for human consumption.

CERT_FRENCH.name: French (Advanced Language Study)
CERT_FRENCH.description: Certificate of Advanced Language Study in French offered by the French Department to Yale College undergraduates who are not French majors.
notes: For non-majors only
No Credit/D/Fail
Letter grade B or above required in all courses
Declare candidacy on Yale Hub as early as possible, no later than January 15 or September 15 of final semester
With DUS approval, one advanced non-L5 course conducted in French (e.g., independent study graded pass/fail or graduate seminar) may count
One LxC course taught in English may count if it includes a weekly discussion section conducted entirely in French and the student completes all readings and assignments in French
Up to two study-abroad courses taught in French may count as electives with DUS approval

requirements.name: Courses beyond L4
requirements.description: Four courses beyond the L4 level in French. At least two must be Yale courses designated L5. At least one must be a French Department course in French in the FREN 2000–4999 range.

CERT_GERMAN.name: German (Advanced Language Study)
CERT_GERMAN.description: Certificate of Advanced Language Study in German offered by the Department of Germanic Languages and Literatures. A certificate adviser, typically the DUS, advises students on the certification process. The certificate is listed on the student transcript once certified.
notes: No Credit/D/Fail

Declare candidacy on Yale Hub as early as possible, no later than January 15 or September 15 of final semester
With adviser approval, one advanced non-L5 course conducted in German (e.g., independent study graded pass/fail, graduate seminar, or advanced seminar) may count

CERT_GLOBAL_HEALTH.name: Global Health Studies
CERT_GLOBAL_HEALTH.description: Prepares students to critically engage with global health and its multifaceted concerns through interdisciplinary coursework across politics, history, economics, anthropology, ethics, law, sociology, public health, and the biomedical sciences.
notes: Students apply to the program, typically in the fall of sophomore year. Accepted students are called Global Health Scholars.

Four electives must fulfill four of six global health competency areas: Biological & Environmental Influences on Health (YC GLHTH Bio & Env Influences); Health & Societies (YC GLHTH Health & Societies); Historical Approaches (YC GLHTH Hist Approaches); Performance, Representation & Health (YC GLHTH Perf, Rep & Health); Political Economy & Governance in Health (YC GLHTH Polit Econ & Govern); Understanding & Interpreting Quantitative Data (YC GLHTH Quantitative Data).
Scholars may apply for funding for mentored experiential learning projects the summer after junior year.
No more than one course taken Credit/D/Fail may count toward the certificate; HLTH 4900 must be taken for a letter grade.
No more than two courses may overlap with a major, simultaneous degree, or another certificate.
No course credit may be applied toward the requirements of more than two curricular programs.
Qualified undergraduates may take graduate courses at the School of Public Health subject to Yale College regulations.
Courses taken at another institution or during an approved summer or term-time study abroad program may count with DUS approval.

requirements.name: Introductory lecture
requirements.description: Global health introductory lecture course.

requirements.name: Competency electives
requirements.description: Four electives achieving four of the six global health competency areas as indicated by course attributes.

requirements.name: Senior colloquium
requirements.description: Senior colloquium integrating skills and knowledge acquired throughout the program. Must be taken for a letter grade.

CERT_HINDI.name: Hindi (Advanced Language Study)
CERT_HINDI.description: Certificate of Advanced Language Study in Hindi offered by the Department of South Asian Studies. A certificate adviser, typically the DUS, advises students on the certification process. The certificate is listed on the student's transcript once certified through Degree Audit.

With adviser approval, one advanced non-L5 Yale course conducted in Hindi (e.g., independent study graded pass/fail, graduate seminar, or advanced seminar) may count
One LxC course taught in English may count if it includes a weekly discussion section conducted entirely in Hindi (minimum three students; course designated LxC)
Up to two study-abroad credits taught in Hindi may be substituted with adviser approval

requirements.name: Courses beyond L4
requirements.description: Four courses beyond the L4 level in Hindi. At least two must be Yale courses designated L5.

CERT_HUMAN_RIGHTS.name: Human Rights Studies
CERT_HUMAN_RIGHTS.description: Available to all interested Yale students, this certificate provides the opportunity to pursue an interdisciplinary study of human rights.
notes: No courses taken Credit/D/Fail may be applied toward the certificate.

Courses taken at another institution or during an approved summer or term-time study abroad program may count with certificate director approval. An on-topic summer internship can replace one elective with approval.
Graduate and professional school courses may count with director approval or if tagged with approved attributes.
Declare on Yale Hub by January 15 or September 15 of the final semester at the latest.

requirements.name: Gateway
requirements.description: Gateway course introducing theoretical tools for studying human rights.

requirements.name: Domestic elective
requirements.description: Elective with YC Human Rights Domestic attribute that substantially engages with human rights language, ideas, and methods.

requirements.name: International elective
requirements.description: Elective with YC Human Rights International attribute that substantially engages with human rights language, ideas, and methods.

requirements.name: Additional electives
requirements.description: Additional human rights electives approved for the certificate.

CERT_HUMAN_RIGHTS_INTENSIVE.name: Human Rights Studies Intensive
CERT_HUMAN_RIGHTS_INTENSIVE.description: An intensive pathway for students who wish to engage deeply with the study of human rights, including regular cohort programming throughout the academic year.
notes: Apply during the spring term of sophomore year only via the Human Rights website.
Students participate in regular (typically weekly) additional programming tailored for the small cohort throughout the academic year.
Non-credited senior colloquium required.
Electives must engage with the language, ideas, and methods of human rights with substantial focus (four or more of thirteen, or six to eight of twenty-six, course meetings per syllabus).
No courses taken Credit/D/Fail may be applied toward the certificate.

Courses taken at another institution or during an approved summer or term-time study abroad program may count with certificate director approval. An on-topic summer internship can replace one elective with approval.
Graduate and professional school courses may count with director approval or if tagged with approved attributes.

requirements.name: Gateway

requirements.name: International elective
requirements.description: Elective with YC Human Rights International attribute.

CERT_ISLAMIC_STUDIES.name: Islamic Studies
CERT_ISLAMIC_STUDIES.description: Encompasses the study of Muslim and Islamic artistic, cultural, historical, intellectual, linguistic, literary, philosophical, political, religious, sociological, and scientific presence and impact on human society over the past one and a half millennia.
notes: No more than two courses may represent the same area of study.
Each student must attend three lectures on topics relating to Islamic Studies and submit a brief 1–2 page write-up for each.

requirements.name: Islamic Society
requirements.description: One approved course in Islamic Society.

CERT_LATIN.description: Certificate of Advanced Language Study in Latin offered by the Classics Department to non-majors. A certificate adviser, typically the DUS, advises students on the certification process. The certificate is listed on the student transcript once certified.
notes: For non-majors only

CERT_NATIVE_AMERICAN_INDIGENOUS.name: Native American and Indigenous Studies
CERT_NATIVE_AMERICAN_INDIGENOUS.description: Offers a curated range of courses across departments and programs in Yale College that center on Indigenous content, strengthening knowledge of Indigenous languages, cultures, sovereignty, history, literatures, and lifeways.
notes: Courses must be drawn from at least three of five areas of focus, with no more than two courses from any single area.

Optional capstone project counts as one credit toward the certificate. Capstone may be completed in an independent study (e.g. LING 4710, ENGL 3100, AMST 9000, SOCY 4100) or upper-division core seminar (ER&M 4020) with director approval. Submit a 1-page proposal in spring of junior year or early fall of senior year.
Students must participate in at least three Indigenous community events and submit a 1–2 page write-up per event.
No courses taken Credit/D/Fail may be counted toward the certificate.
No more than two course credits may overlap with a major, simultaneous degree, or another certificate.

CERT_PERSIAN_IRANIAN.name: Persian and Iranian Studies
CERT_PERSIAN_IRANIAN.description: Recognizes undergraduates who combine the study of Persian language and literature with wider engagement with the art, philosophy, religion, history, politics, and culture of the Persian-speaking world.

All courses must be taken for a letter grade of B or above.
Only two content courses should originate in the same department.
Persian L5 courses are content-oriented and may count as either a content or language course.
Premodern Iranian language courses (e.g. Old Persian, Middle Persian, Soghdian) count as content courses.
